intro: Taxonomy change today: software and IT-services names with a live generative-AI substitution debate (Adobe, ServiceNow, SAP, Wolters Kluwer, Intuit, Accenture, Salesforce, IBM, Alphabet, Uber) now carry their own AI-EXPOSED durability class instead of being filed under 'durable'. That is why the compounder list shrank and the AI-fear basket appeared — the price rules did not change.

notes.ORCL: Oracle tops the ranking on mechanics: the stock sits within 2% of the model's own $144 BEAR scenario after the BBB- downgrade scare, so Ratio B rounds to zero and the model-vs-market gap is +1.94. The franchise (database + OCI, $30B+ of new AI cloud contracts) is durable; the risk is financing — $40B of debt plus a $20B equity raise this fiscal year. Buy, but size it as an AI-capex bet, not a bond proxy.
notes.SYK: Stryker 1.5% above its EPP floor with 0.22x Ratio B and a +1.11 gap — a medtech compounder at the floor is the cleanest quality-at-a-low-price setup in the book.
notes.TMUS: T-Mobile: still the best combination of durability and asymmetry — 0.30x Ratio B, +1.49 gap, 96% upside to bull versus 29% downside. Capital-intensive oligopoly, nothing here becomes useless.
notes.HD: Home Depot at 0.15x Ratio B, 7% above floor, conservative 2-yr +34%. A frozen housing market is a trough for a durable franchise, not a broken one.
notes.MRSH: Marsh McLennan 7% above floor at 0.22x Ratio B; the CEO transition (Matt Stadler, Sept 16) is worth watching but the fee-based moat and 19-year margin streak are intact.
notes.PEG: PSEG pushed toward a 52-week low on rate sensitivity — now 0.5% above its floor with 0.33x Ratio B and guidance reaffirmed. Regulated wires plus nuclear; obsolescence risk as low as equities get.
notes.SPGI: S&P Global 11.5% BELOW its own panic floor at 0.20x Ratio B — a ratings duopoly plus index flywheel below the floor. Buy on safety first, upside second.
notes.KKR: KKR: +1.01 gap, 0.43x Ratio B, conservative 2-yr +17%. Fee-related earnings durable, realizations cyclical — size below MRSH and SPGI.
notes.AZO: AutoZone 13% above floor at 0.20x Ratio B into the Sept 22 print. Counter-cyclical buyback compounder; the EV mix headwind is decade-scale.
notes.WM: Waste Management at 0.40x Ratio B, +0.93 gap; landfill moat with pricing power. The floor distance (+75%) is the only thing keeping it out of the top five.
notes.SNY: Sanofi at the low end of its range, 16% above floor, 0.38x Ratio B, conservative 2-yr +34% — the cheapest durable large pharma in coverage.
notes.AXP: American Express 0.38x Ratio B, +0.72 gap, conservative 2-yr +17%; the closed-loop network keeps compounding, credit cycle is the swing.
notes.MA: Mastercard: +0.81 gap but Ratio B only 0.91x — quality at a fair-to-good price rather than a bargain.
notes.SCHW: Schwab: +0.90 gap, 0.72x Ratio B; cash-sorting relief is the tailwind, rate cuts the risk.
notes.BX: Blackstone: 0.59x Ratio B, +0.83 gap; same caveat as KKR — fee earnings durable, realizations cyclical.
notes.TT: Trane: +0.98 gap and 0.45x Ratio B on the data-center cooling cycle; 92% above a trough-EPS floor is the reason it is second line, not first.
notes.ADBE: Adobe 7.5% BELOW its floor at 0.23x Ratio B after a beat-and-raise (AI-first ARR $650M) — the market's clearest 'generative-AI loser' bet. The numbers keep refusing it; the CEO transition (Dec 1) is the next test. Core of the basket.
notes.SAP: SAP: +0.94 gap, 0.68x Ratio B; the system-of-record is sticky, the debate is whether the Joule agent layer ships (17 of 200 agents delivered). Lower AI risk than the rest of the basket.
notes.NOW: ServiceNow at $136 after the software-sector selloff: 0.43x Ratio B, +0.59 gap, 102% upside to bull. Per-seat licensing versus agentic AI is unresolved — the purest expression of the fear.
notes.WKL: Wolters Kluwer 16% above floor at 0.68x Ratio B; renewal numbers keep refusing the AI-disruption thesis. Information services are where substitution is most plausible, so it stays in the basket.
notes.INTU: Intuit 10% above floor, 0.48x Ratio B, conservative 2-yr +37%, but the composite reads fairly valued and AI tax-prep is a direct substitute for TurboTax. In the basket on price, not on conviction.
notes.ACN: Accenture: 0.45x Ratio B, fairly valued composite, Guggenheim downgrade on weak organic growth and falling job listings. GenAI deflates IT-services pricing and Accenture is also the delivery partner for it — both sides of the trade in one name.
notes.GOOGL: Alphabet: modestly undervalued but 81% above floor at 1.2x Ratio B; AI-search cannibalisation versus Gemini/TPU. Wait for the discount.
notes.CRM: Salesforce at 1.76x Ratio B with a flat composite — AI-exposed and not cheap enough to pay for the Agentforce bet.
notes.IBM: IBM: consulting is the AI-deflation exposure, composite -0.61; not cheap.
notes.UBER: Uber: 1.45x Ratio B, fairly valued; autonomous vehicles are partner and existential threat at once. No margin of safety for that debate.
notes.FISV: Fiserv at a 12-year-style low, 34% BELOW its floor with 0.02x Ratio B — but merchant growth is decelerating and the M&A premium is gone. Turnaround, not compounder.
notes.NKE: Nike at a 12-year low, 11% below a floor computed on collapsed earnings. A bet on new management, not a value buy.
notes.CMCSA: Comcast: statistically the cheapest name in coverage and still out of the buy list — broadband keeps losing subscribers to fixed-wireless and fiber, so the E in the floor is eroding.
notes.CHTR: Charter: same cable share-loss problem as Comcast plus leverage; the model's BUY is a price mechanic.
notes.EIX: Edison below its floor because California's wildfire-liability regime is uncapped; the tail is legislative, not financial. Binary.
notes.TSLA: Tesla: auto earnings collapsed, price is the robotaxi option; the worst risk/reward in coverage on the model's own numbers.
notes.TRGP: Targa 500%+ above its panic floor; the midstream premium has nothing left to price.
notes.MPC: Marathon Petroleum on a geopolitical crack-spread spike at a fresh high; the Street's own targets sit below spot.
notes.AAPL: Apple with the memory-cost margin question unresolved into the Oct 29 print, 100%+ above floor; conservative case deeply negative.
notes.DE: Deere at an all-time high on ~40x trough-cycle EPS; conservative 2-yr case -44%.
notes.META: Meta after the settlement rally: 15x Ratio B, 100% above floor — the ad engine is healthy, the price is the problem.
notes.PLTR: Palantir 290% above floor at 5.8x Ratio B; exceptional business, no margin of safety versus a genuine bear case.
notes.AMD: AMD ~200% above floor; the AI ramp has to be flawless and the conservative case is -47%.

sectors.Technology: Split three ways now: the AI-fear basket (ADBE, NOW, SAP, WKL, INTU, ACN) is where the discount lives; ORCL, ADYEN, NFLX and PRX are durable compounders at a low price; MSFT, META, PLTR, PANW, AVGO and the semis (AMD, MRVL, ASML, LRCX) are priced for perfection or at a cycle peak. NVDA and MU are cyclicals with the risk partly priced.
sectors.Finance: The deepest pool of durable value in coverage: MRSH, SPGI, KKR, AXP, BX, SCHW and MA are compounders at a low price; BAC, PGR, SAN and C are cyclicals with the risk priced in. The EU retail banks at highs (INGA, ISP, UCG, NDA, DBK) still carry too much cycle risk with one shared failure mode — deposit-margin compression before fee growth offsets it.
sectors.Healthcare: SYK and SNY are the compounders at a low price; the patent-cliff names (BMY, PFE) stay structurally challenged, and LLY, VRTX, ISRG, ARGX are priced for perfection.
sectors.Utilities: PEG is the regulated compounder at a low price; CEG and VST are cyclicals with the risk priced in; EIX and PCG remain special situations on wildfire liability.

dangers: Crowding at highs. 49 quality names and 46 cyclicals are priced for perfection or at a cycle peak — 42% of coverage. The largest single risk remains buying good companies at the top of their ranges.

The AI trade, both sides. The AI-fear basket (ADBE, NOW, SAP, WKL, INTU, ACN) and the AI-capex winners (NVDA, AMD, MRVL, AVGO, PLTR, VST, CEG, TT, ETN) are mirror images of one debate. A capex digestion phase hits them in opposite directions; a software-sector selloff like this week's hits the basket regardless of the numbers.
Cheap-for-a-reason. Cable (CMCSA, CHTR), California utilities (EIX, PCG), Fiserv and Nike screen cheapest in coverage; in every case the E in the floor is contested. They are labelled, not promoted.

Rate sensitivity on the buy side. PEG, SCHW, TMUS and the regulated names on the buy list all lose if long rates keep rising; the EU banks on the sell list lose if they fall. The book is not neutral to the rate path.
